sourceDerivedProof.choice1: Native figure marks angle ADB=50°, angle AXB=95°, angle DBC=45°. Since A,X,C are collinear, angle BXC=85°. Triangle BXC gives angle ACB=angle BCX=50°, equal to angle ADB; equal inscribed angles subtend chord AB, so A,B,C,D are cyclic.
sourceDerivedProof.choice2: The two chords AC and BD intersect at E. Native labels give AE=2, ED=3, BE=4, EC=6. AE×EC=2×6=12=4×3=BE×ED, so the converse of the intersecting-chords theorem gives cyclicity.
sourceDerivedProof.choice3: Native marks show AB parallel DC and AD=BC, so ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid. Its base angles are equal and consecutive angles are supplementary; opposite angles are supplementary, so ABCD is cyclic.
sourceDerivedProof.choice4: Native labels give angle BAC=55° and angle BCA=45°, hence angle ABC=80°. The other opposite angle ADC=100°, so angle ABC+angle ADC=180° and ABCD is cyclic.
sourceDerivedProof.choice5: Native diagram shows P,D,A collinear and P,C,B collinear, with PD=3, DA=4, PC=2, CB=6. Thus PA=7 and PB=8. If A,B,C,D were cyclic, secant power would require PA×PD=PB×PC; but 7×3=21 while 8×2=16. Therefore choice ⑤ is the only configuration that is not cyclic.

currentSourceDisposition: Independent source proof identifies option ⑤ as the only noncyclic case. Current artifact answer is ③; current solution SHA is the earlier incorrect proof treating option ③ as a general parallelogram despite equal-leg marks.
